name: Queue Implemented Using Stack(s)
recognitionClueHinglish: Code/design diya hai jo do stacks (ya ek stack + extra op) use karke Queue implement karta hai — poocha hai correctness, minimum stacks needed, ya operation trace. Ye is topic ka sabse bada pattern hai (15 me se 5 PYQs).
whatShouldComeToMind: Minimum 2 stacks needed for a correct queue via plain push/pop.
Standard design: S1 for incoming (enqueue = push to S1), S2 for outgoing (dequeue = pop from S2; if S2 empty, pour ALL of S1 into S2 first).
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Identify which stack receives ENQUEUEs (usually S1) and which serves DEQUEUEs (usually S2).
2. Trace operations explicitly: enqueue → push S1. dequeue → if S2 empty, pop everything off S1 and push onto S2 (this REVERSES order back to FIFO), then pop S2's top.
3. For 'minimum stacks' questions, recall that 1 stack alone cannot do it — 2 is the proven minimum.
variationsObserved: peek-style operations (front of queue without removing) combined with the two-stack design.
commonTraps: Pouring S1 into S2 even when S2 is NOT empty — this breaks FIFO order (should only pour when S2 is empty).
edgeCases: Dequeue on an empty queue (both stacks empty) — must be handled/checked explicitly.

name: Circular Queue Array Implementation
recognitionClueHinglish: Array-based circular queue diya hai, front/rear index variables ke saath, aur poocha hai full/empty condition kya hai, ya efficient enqueue/dequeue ke baare me statement TRUE hai ya nahi.
whatShouldComeToMind: next index = (current+1) mod capacity — the core wraparound formula.
front==rear is AMBIGUOUS (could mean empty OR full) — needs a count variable, a sacrificed slot, or a flag to disambiguate.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Apply the modulo formula for index updates on enqueue/dequeue.
2. For full/empty questions, check which disambiguation scheme is implied and reason accordingly.
3. For 'can both operations be O(1)' questions — yes, with a good circular array design, both are O(1).
commonTraps: Not accounting for the front==rear ambiguity between full and empty states.

name: Linked-List Based Queue Implementation
recognitionClueHinglish: Queue linked list se implement kiya gaya hai (head/tail pointers ke saath, ya sirf ek pointer ke saath) aur poocha hai enqueue/dequeue ki efficiency (O(1) vs O(n)) kya hogi.
whatShouldComeToMind: Both head AND tail pointers maintained → both enqueue (at tail) and dequeue (at head) are O(1).
Only ONE pointer (say just head) maintained, and enqueue happens at the 'far' end → that operation degrades to O(n) (must traverse to find the end).
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Check exactly which pointers (head only? head+tail? circular with one pointer to tail?) are maintained.
2. For each operation (enqueue/dequeue), determine if it can be done by direct pointer access (O(1)) or needs traversal (O(n)).
variationsObserved: Circular linked list with a SINGLE pointer to the REAR node (clever trick: rear->next gives front) — both operations still O(1) despite only one external pointer.
commonTraps: Assuming a single pointer always means one operation is O(n) — the circular-with-rear-pointer trick is a specific exception worth recognizing.

name: Conceptual / Theoretical Queue Statements
recognitionClueHinglish: TRUE/FALSE statements about FIFO vs LIFO efficiency, ya ek DS design karna hai for a specific constant-time-operations requirement — ye conceptual/design pattern hai, calculation kam, theory zyada.
whatShouldComeToMind: FIFO = Queue's job, NOT Stack's (Stack is LIFO) — a direct mislabeling is a classic false-statement trap.
For custom DS design questions (like 'subset of 1..n with O(1) ops'), think about what auxiliary array/bit-vector could give O(1) membership/insert/delete.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. For TRUE/FALSE statements, carefully verify which structure (stack/queue/list) each claim is actually about.
2. For open-ended DS-design questions, think about direct-indexed arrays (bit-vectors) for O(1) access when the domain is bounded (like 1..n).
variationsObserved: A composite/derived queue operation (like MultiDequeue removing up to k elements) — analyze via amortized analysis across a full SEQUENCE of operations, not a single call.
commonTraps: Mislabeling FIFO/LIFO between stack and queue.
Analyzing a composite operation's worst case PER CALL instead of amortized over a sequence, leading to an overly pessimistic bound.

name: Queue Operation Sequence Tracing
recognitionClueHinglish: Ek sequence of enqueue/dequeue (ya insertFirst/removeLast style deque operations) di hai aur poocha hai final state/count/output kya hoga — direct tracing pattern.
whatShouldComeToMind: Maintain an explicit queue (ordered list, front and rear marked) and process every operation literally.
For deques (double-ended queues), track BOTH ends and process insert/remove-first/last operations carefully.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Draw the queue explicitly (or deque, with both ends marked).
2. Process every operation in order, updating the drawing.
variationsObserved: Minimum number of a SPECIFIC operation needed to transform one queue-state into another — a reachability/counting question, not a pure simulation.
commonTraps: Mixing up 'insertFirst/removeLast' style deque operations with plain FIFO enqueue/dequeue.
